abstract: How do recommendation algorithms contribute to the formation of polarized opinions in online social networks? This question has been studied through empirical analyses of real platforms and mathematical models of opinion dynamics. Empirical studies capture user behavior but are often limited by noisy, incomplete, or inaccessible platform data, while mathematical models offer control and interpretability but usually rely on simplified opinion update rules. More recently, large language model (LLM)-based social simulations have provided an alternative for studying recommendation and opinion dynamics through natural-language interactions. However, how different ways of applying recommendations shape opinion dynamics remains underexplored.   In this work, we provide a controlled comparison of two different recommendation mechanisms in an LLM-based online social network simulation. Edge Recommendation (ER) introduces new connections in the network, while Content-Exposure Recommendation (CR) exposes additional users to individual posts without modifying the underlying graph. Our framework represents users as LLM-based agents who interact in natural language while maintaining evolving opinion states. We measure polarization as opinion dispersion, extremization as the average distance of opinions from the neutral midpoint, and reinforcement as interactions that amplify already aligned opinions. Our results show higher mean polarization and extremization across recommendation conditions compared with the no-recommendation baseline, with absolute differences of up to $0.12$ in our main experiments.

ur.ai_reason: LLM社交模拟研究推荐算法对极化的影响，含用户行为建模
ur.tldr: 研究推荐算法如何影响社交网络意见极化。基于LLM构建在线社交网络仿真平台，对比边推荐(ER)与内容曝光推荐(CR)两种机制，用户作为LLM智能体以自然语言交互并维持动态意见状态。以意见离散度衡量极化、极化端衡量极端化、互动放大衡量强化。结果显示推荐条件下平均极化与极端化程度更高。

title: Polarization Dynamics under Algorithmic Recommendations in LLM-based Online Social Networks
title_zh: 基于LLM的在线社交网络中算法推荐下的极化动态
